status: reviewed against exact pinned source; three-step undo and redo development probe passed on Linux/macOS; qualification pending
findings: The C-x keymap binds lowercase u to undo.
undo.c records inverse operations during undo; its undo pointer points at the preceding action after an undo.
The pinned source comment says that when the pointer reaches the bottom or moves between undo actions, the pointer returns to the newest record; this is how the command performs redo.

The native probe passed on Linux and macOS: deletion changes the suffix, first C-x u restores it, second C-x u consumes the MODIFIED marker without changing text, and third C-x u redoes the deletion. Both runs passed exact public-spec screen checkpoints and the same-invocation final file-state assertion.
C-x u is bound to undo; the source also binds Ctrl-_ to undo, but the probe uses the documented prefix binding.
safety: synthetic disposable file, secure mode -S and backups disabled with -n
